author: Development Codex session 10
title: Isolated Robot-Codex readiness RCI001-wsl-010c
summary: Exact bounded development source and configuration; actual qualification is recorded separately.
mechanism:
# Filesystem-native recovery inside an enforced invocation boundary

The normal worker remains the frozen r4 Panda/MuJoCo machine-tending controller. It chooses native skills from public observations until its existing help rule activates recovery. A protected supervisor then gives one fresh Robot-Codex invocation a capability for the current task and authority generation. The agent reads the configured filesystem, investigates the incident, requests bounded operations, checks public feedback, and asks the supervisor to return control. The independent evaluator remains outside the agent's filesystem and observations.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[Conventional controller] --> S[Protected supervisor\nExclusive ownership and action registry]
  S --> P[Native r4 skills and actuators\nMuJoCo physics continues]
  P --> O[Public sensing and receipts]
  O --> S
  L[Trusted Windows launcher\nExisting ChatGPT authentication\nAstra Max] --> E[WSL2 bubblewrap executor\nFresh invocation and isolated Code Mode]
  E --> W[Configured filesystem\nRead-only tasks and live records\nWritable notes, programs, continuity]
  E --> B[Fixed broker\nExact robot routes only]
  B --> S
  L --> F[Separate protected lifecycle API\nStart, retire, stop]
  F --> S
```

The sole model input is `Follow the instructions in RobotAgentPrompt.md.`. Automatic project instructions, skills, memory, apps, MCP tools, web, local execution and subagents are disabled. Effective configuration and actual dispatch are retained; this is not an exhaustive exported live model-tool schema. The installed Windows client holds authentication. No account credential is read, copied into WSL, or substituted with an API key.

Both the Linux executor and Code Mode host have separate bubblewrap namespaces. Windows drives, user homes, repository, reference plans, evaluator, concealed development manifests and ambient networking are absent. Read-only system runtime libraries support command execution. The broker accepts only fixed status/history/query/observation/continuity/command/handback routes, validates bounded JSON and keeps the upstream origin and token fixed for that invocation. Operator routes never enter this broker. Structured robot observations are available; model image viewing remains disabled, even though requested public image artifacts can be retained.

The protected owner thread alone changes the simulator. It admits commands with stable request IDs, current authority/task revision, fresh observation sequence, native limits and equipment interlocks. It retains requests before dispatch and separates requested, admitted/executing, terminal, and public post-action support. A receipt is not proof of a grasp, placement or task success. Uncertain commands are queried; the client does not silently retry or acquire a new authority generation.

The OS boundary supports agent-written shell/Python. A documented Python runner seals a versioned source snapshot before execution, retains its admitted hash/bytes before process creation, limits source/output/time and per-child memory, and retires detached descendants. Its final receipt is separate; an admission with no final outcome remains unknown. This is a convenience within the invocation's permissions, not a second privilege boundary. All scripts share the same gateway limits and cannot create a persistent controller outside namespace retirement. There is no dedicated privileged program service or simulator/driver access.

The launcher owns the invocation deadline. A separate protected capability starts and retires invocations; the public agent cannot call it. Retirement revokes robot access and fences already queued requests, while restart preserves action budgets and unresolved outcomes. The launcher must verify all prior executor/Code Mode namespaces retired before admitting a fresh thread. After handback, retirement preserves newly resumed conventional motion. Old tokens remain unusable even if the old client saved them.

Runtime backing lives under a dedicated WSL `/var/tmp` directory. The public `Continuity.md` is a fixed symlink to a file inside a writable directory, so atomic replacement becomes visible without replacing a bind-mounted inode. The protected continuity service saves old and newly committed notes before acknowledging them; the broker atomically publishes the committed bytes into WSL. Fresh invocation initialization uses the protected committed note and retains older local bytes separately for reconciliation. Public state/activation/structured-observation mirrors refresh while the simulator advances. Actual HTTP status/history remains the current public interface.

The trusted harness fsyncs model and broker traces, exports bounded actual runtime bytes even after client failure, and compares retained hashes after namespace/broker teardown. Each tested revision has an immutable source archive and attempt manifest in the Architecture Map. Dynamic runtime input hashes, effective binary/configuration evidence, queue receipts and independent assessments identify the exact attempt. Old failed native and WSL attempts are preserved.

This architecture supports bounded simulation development, not physical deployment or a scored release by itself. Full supervisor/computer restart recovery, power-loss recovery, disk-full operation, aggregate resource exhaustion, complete whole-arm/contact protection and general recovery performance are unqualified. A host crash terminates and invalidates the episode; it does not automatically restart a possibly ambiguous physical task. Resource/deadline failures retain their outcome and require operator handling. The single authorized development pilot cannot estimate performance, and no campaign starts without Randy's review.

title: Isolated Robot-Codex readiness RCI001-C02-dev-001
summary: Exact bounded development source and configuration; actual qualification is recorded separately.
mechanism:
# Campaign 002: apparatus repair and known-fixture repeatability

Randy's September 27, 2026 13:45 PDT instruction authorizes infrastructure repair, requalification and this campaign without another launch approval. Campaign 001 remains exactly 6 valid successes, 4 infrastructure-invalid attempts and 14 not run. Its sources, manifests, assessments and investigation are immutable inputs, not targets for repair.

## Experiment and allocation

After qualification, run **20 fresh attempts, 10 per known challenge family**: misplaced stock and blocked insert home. Keep world seed 173, use sensor seeds 23001–23020, alternate family within pairs and reverse first family on alternate pairs. Use a fresh external workspace, empty initial continuity and one fresh GPT-6 Astra Max invocation per slot. The exact sole bootstrap remains `Follow the instructions in RobotAgentPrompt.md.`. No recovery prompt, template, policy, controller, physics, sensing, fixture or evaluator tuning is authorized here.

Campaign 001's ten starts occupied 49.10 queue minutes and 46.71 summed host minutes; 6 were valid and 4 infrastructure-invalid. A 20-slot allocation projects approximately 98 minutes of queue occupancy at that observed mean, plus qualification, reporting and service variability. The host caps allow up to 6.11 hours of physics-host time, with outer overhead additional. Ten trials per family have an 89.3% chance to expose at least one event of probability 20%, assuming independent trials; 10/10 successes still have a 95% Wilson lower limit near 72.2%. This is useful repeatability evidence with broad uncertainty, not a high-reliability certification. Twenty is a fresh allocation justified by observed cost and precision, not replacement of Campaign 001's fourteen unrun slots.

## Repairs and prospective timing definition

The transport repair makes established revocation durable in the broker: a confirmed handback or definitive denial of the pinned capability latches local denial of later calls. It never fabricates successful continuity, extends robot authority, or forgives an unexplained transport failure. New request-intent and failure records retain route, association and time.

Campaign 001 used a per-tick loop origin and a differently anchored sparse journal reconstruction. Home02 passed the former and failed the latter; home03/home05 failed both. Campaign 002 retains complete compact timing samples with one explicit measured-physics origin and samples before catch-up as well as after ticks. Apply the **unchanged** frozen TimingMonitor: maximum lag strictly below 0.1 s, one-second RTF 0.95–1.05, and strictly fewer than 1% out-of-range windows. Initialization before physics and terminal cleanup after it are explicitly outside the interval, as the original monitor specification intended. Journal reconstruction remains diagnostic. This is a prospective measurement correction, not a reinterpretation of Campaign 001.

The initial stabilization uses existing WSL service warmup before host start, Windows AboveNormal host priority and a paired 1 ms timer request, with receipts. These are prospective scheduling changes, not proven explanations of historical stalls. Per-phase measurements will identify any remaining critical-path delays. A failed development qualification can lead to another infrastructure revision with a new immutable run identity; every failure remains retained. No scored outcomes may be used for tuning.

## Qualification gates

Before scoring, register and freeze each tested revision. Run meaningful negative tests for revocation, transport errors, source/queue integrity, timing replay and threshold equality. Preserve existing host, client, boundary, lifecycle, evaluator and continuity tests. Run six unretried no-model reference episodes (three per family, sensor seeds 24001–24006) through the shared queue to test the repaired host and independently verified fixture completion. Retain every failed qualification, never silently replace it.

Then exercise the full isolated path with the existing interruption/fresh-invocation smoke and one development pilot per family (seeds 24101–24103, fresh identities). The smoke has its existing two-invocation lifecycle protocol; pilots retain the campaign's one-invocation protocol. Require authentic queue completion, original boundary canaries, control fencing, complete evidence/retirement/continuity, independent evaluation, and strict fresh timing for the final revision. Diagnostic retries after a repair are distinct new qualification attempts, not scored repetitions. If these gates cannot be satisfied, scoring stays closed and the concrete unresolved evidence is reported.

Seal the exact final implementation, external assessor, qualification receipts, storage policy, allocation and manifests before any scored launch, then register every scored slot. Implementation changes after a scored start terminate Campaign 002 for review.

## Outcomes, stopping and resources

Keep the 900 simulation-second / 1100 host-wall-second caps, 600-second model invocation, 150-second conventional follow-through, 20 action requests, 50 observations and 512 MiB host evidence cap. Physics advances while the agent reasons. # Campaign 003 candidate: creating and carrying forward a C capability

Development authority: Randy's 2026-10-03 Campaign 003 instruction. This candidate is for review. No Robot-Codex/Astra invocation, model pilot, scored attempt, final campaign freeze or launch is authorized by this package. Campaigns 001 and 002 remain immutable.

## Task and continuity

The existing Panda workcell receives a family C cuboid and a marked C destination. C has the same contact geometry and material parameters as an existing A parcel. A/B machining, sensing, arm, servos, limits, physics timestep and authority interface retain their original sources. C needs only placement, not an invented machining recipe. The conventional worker asks for assistance for C; its task skills refuse C and C_pad. Robot-Codex can use the same bounded joint, trajectory, Cartesian and gripper interface available before C.

Fixed pad geometry is public workcell knowledge. No grasp sequence, approach coordinates, joint solution, generated program, developer demonstration or future schedule is present in the robot template. Developer reachability checks live in the operator-only qualification tree. C initialization and later reloading are declared plant/job events; recovery never edits object poses, welds an object, or changes hardware.

An eventual block contains at least three C encounters, separated by conventional work and freshly created robot threads/process namespaces. The protected scheduler samples gaps and releases only the current job. All notes, programs and canonical continuity survive. Conversation history, provider response IDs, model context, process memory, scratch files and hidden reasoning do not. The public task says only that C may recur in later jobs. It neither requests a reusable program nor directs a memory strategy. The normal file-ownership and factual-evidence rules still apply.

## Predeclared outcome distinctions

Each encounter has a separate task outcome and infrastructure validity. Immediate C success requires protected geometry: the entire C footprint inside the pad, resting height within 6 mm, speed below 0.02 m/s, open jaws, TCP at least 0.09 m away, sustained for one simulation second; then an accepted handback and authoritative conventional-resumption receipt. Motion completion or an agent claim does not establish placement.

Artifact existence alone is not knowledge transfer. Record separately: first successful placement; created/modified artifacts; later read/execute events with exact content hashes; correspondence between retained information and subsequent actions; outcome; tool/action counts; elapsed simulation/wall time; rejected requests; image inspection. Reuse means a prior encounter's content-bearing artifact was read or executed before a relevant later decision and its concrete content corresponds to the subsequent action. Useful transfer additionally requires valid later success and observable use of task-relevant prior information. Label the causal contribution unknown without a matched withholding intervention, which this candidate does not authorize.

Rediscovery is supported only when complete evidence shows a new derivation without relevant retained-content use. If behavior is ambiguous, classify unknown, not rediscovery or transfer. A durable procedure/program requires retained executable or sufficiently operational content; later successful execution/use is a separate outcome. Abstraction is optional, not necessary for immediate success. The three encounters are correlated within one persistent block, not three independent samples. No model-performance result exists from deterministic qualification.

## Prospective validity and stopping

Keep the original strict timing limits: maximum lag <100 ms, one-second RTF in [0.95,1.05], fewer than 1% bad windows. Physics continues during reasoning, journal writes and tool execution. Keep exclusive authority, request identity, stale-observation rejection, durable intent before dispatch, independent evaluator, isolated executor and verified namespace retirement. Host crashes, uncertain dispatch, missing journal operations/content, clock gaps, incomplete retirement, wrong runtime/model/source or actual forbidden exposure invalidate the encounter and stop admission. Preserve unknown physical outcomes. Never silently restart an ambiguous operation or replace an invalid slot.

Candidate limits: 900 simulation seconds and 1100 wall seconds per C encounter; 600 seconds per model invocation; <=20 physical requests and <=50 explicit observations per activation; manual horizon <=2 seconds. Three minimum C encounters use separate activations. Workspace limit 256 MiB, each file <=16 MiB, protected journal budget 1 GiB per block, host evidence <=512 MiB per encounter. Keep 100 GB native free reserve and 2 GB retirement headroom. Quota failures fail closed with retained evidence and no success label. A valid ineffective agent may fail the task; infrastructure failures remain distinct. Final allocation, seeds, repetition count and exact source freeze require Randy's review.

## Evidence

Retain rendered image bytes and capture/publication/view identities; structured sensor packets; public model messages and tool input/output; robot request/admission/dispatch/feedback; authority and handback transitions; world timing anchors; exact initial workspace and mutation records; and final state before/after retirement. Hidden reasoning and credentials are excluded at capture. Machine-authored terminal continuity records are separate from agent claims and never trigger a model wakeup.

The exact journal contract, deployment checks and measured limitations belong in EVIDENCE.md and the qualification receipt. Readiness claims must follow those receipts rather than this proposed contract.
